prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: العربية · المنتجات (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 4 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "المنتج" · longest unbreakable word 50px · one-line width 97px
  col 2: header "السعر" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 70px
  col 3: header "المخزون" · longest unbreakable word 53px · one-line width 53px
  col 4: header "الوصف" · longest unbreakable word 57px · one-line width 445px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 440px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 439px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

These are all candidate designs you produced, rendered in a real browser:
Design r1A: widths [118, 66, 74, 181] · table 440×368px · row heights [36, 106, 60, 106, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [112, 66, 74, 187] · table 440×322px · row heights [36, 83, 60, 83, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2A: widths [112, 91, 74, 162] · table 440×345px · row heights [36, 106, 60, 106, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [118, 91, 74, 156] · table 440×322px · row heights [36, 106, 36, 106, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [100, 91, 74, 174] · table 440×345px · row heights [36, 106, 60, 106, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3A: widths [122, 91, 74, 152] · table 440×322px · row heights [36, 106, 36, 106, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3B: widths [118, 96, 78, 147] · table 440×322px · row heights [36, 106, 36, 106, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3C: widths [112, 91, 74, 162] · table 440×345px · row heights [36, 106, 60, 106, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0

Decide as a designer:
- "preferred": the best design(s). Name more than one only if they are genuinely equally good.
- "acceptable": other designs a careful designer would still publish.
- "bad": designs with clear visual faults, each with the fault. If none of these is clearly bad, also return ONE deliberately bad but plausible alternative as "contrast" widths and say what is wrong with it.
- "ranges": for each column, the px range within which the preferred design stays equally good (keep other columns' proportions).
- "rationale": 2–4 concrete sentences about this table.
- "principles": observations that seem GENERAL (likely to hold for other tables) vs SPECIFIC to this case.
- "tradeoffs" and "uncertain": what reasonable designers could disagree on.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"preferred":["name"],"acceptable":["name"],"bad":[{"design":"name","why":""}],"contrast":{"widths":[int px],"why":""} or null,"ranges":[[min,max]],"rationale":"","principles":{"general":[""],"specific":[""]},"tradeoffs":"","uncertain":""}

the 181px description still needs 4 lines, so the extra width buys nothing and the table grows to 368px."},{"design":"r1B","why":"Same price fault (66px splits number from ر.س) plus a 112px product column that wraps names like \"سماعات لاسلكية\" and \"لوحة مفاتيح\" onto two lines;
